newsitem.title: USA: U.S stocks seen dipping at open after 7 day streak. [CORRECTED 15:54 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks seen dipping at open after 7 day streak. [CORRECTED 15:54 GMT]

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open slightly (corrects by inserting dropped words "were expected to") lower Friday, awaiting some key economic data, after last night's fireworks, when the Dow Industrials, Nasdaq Composite, and the Standard & Poors 500 Index all hit new record high closings.

It was the first time ever the Dow topped the 6300 mark, and its seventh consecutive new closing high, matching a record set in February 5 to 13 earlier this year. "We've got some economic news coming, and with the expiration of options, we'll probably see stocks open a bit on the weak side," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The long bond was off 4/32 to yield 6.43 percent and Standard & Poor's December futures fell 0.35 to 738.9 ahead of the opening of trading.
Hildegard Zagorski, Prudential Securities analyst, said, "It looks like a lower opening, but we seem to open lower and mixed every morning lately."

The market will probably continue to go higher. Right now I just don't see any end to it," she said.

At 0915 EST/1415 GMT, the government will release October industrial production, which economists expect to be flat, and capacity use, forecast to drop to 83.0 percent from 83.3 percent in the prior month.

But Cardillo expressed doubts about how long the party

could go on. "Today, I see a higher opening, but that should take us very much to the top of this run. I think we should see a pullback of a minimum to 200 to 250 points on the down side, concentrated in the Dow stocks," he said.
Tokyo stocks closed slightly lower in thin trading after giving up early gains, with the Nikkei 225 share index off 101 points to about 20,930.
London's FTSE-100 stock index was at session highs, up 28.5 to 3954.6. U.S. stocks trading in London were mixed, with General Motors dropping 1/4 to 55-3/8.

GM said late Thursday it expected recent strikes and its new union contract to cut its fourth quarter earnings by $870 million. It also said profit margins at its Delco Electronics unit were substantially hurt by price cuts and the loss of GM-related business. GM shares closed at 55-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange Thursday.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street analyzes stocks that address the year 2000 problems for computers. Russia's telecommunications company Vimpel is the focus of the New York Times Market Place column. The company is making its debut on the New York Stock Exchange later today.
